A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable methods, equations, evaluations, figures, tables and appendices. The added pose-control material and relocated motion-magnification material can be distinguished reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original DAVIS evaluations, a human preference study, training-density ablations and qualitative video-generation results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds qualitative human-pose-control sequences in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Appendix D adds a pose-specific prompt-construction procedure: estimate human keypoints, animate selected keypoints and convert them into conditioning tracks. The learned ControlNet, training loss and sinusoidal embedding recipe in Appendix A.1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds explicit articulated human-pose control using estimated keypoints (Appendix D/Fig. A3). The training dataset, DAVIS evaluation and existing applications, including motion magnification, are retained.

E2.justification: The DAVIS and human-study comparisons retain Image Conductor and DragAnything. Newly cited methods such as I2VControl and Trajectory Attention are discussed as related work, not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: The DAVIS split, track-count sweeps, metrics, training settings and single-trajectory 2AFC study design are retained. The new pose demonstration introduces no separately specified scoring, sampling or evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Fig. A3 adds a qualitative case study of controlling human joint motion through pose-derived tracks, illustrated by three sequences. Existing track-density ablations, failure examples, training diagnostics and motion-magnification analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 95% confidence intervals in Table 2 and participant counts of 103, 103 and 115. Appendix A.9 retains the single-random-sample generation procedure; no new uncertainty or repeated-run reporting appears.

E6.justification: v2 adds three qualitative human-pose-control sequences. Numerical entries in Tables 1-3 and A2, the training curves in Fig. A2, and existing qualitative results are unchanged. Motion-magnification results are retained as Fig. A4.

T1.justification: The trajectory and visibility definitions and conditioning equation (1) are unchanged. The revised embedding explanation is consistent with Appendix A.1 in both versions; no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about flexible trajectory conditioning, motion prompt expansion, multiple control applications and emergent physical behavior. Pose-control examples add support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly interprets temporally sparse conditioning as predicting subsequent motion after a brief user input, using the existing hair-pulling example. The broader model-probing arguments and Section 4.6 failure and limitation discussion remain.

D1.justification: Detailed implementation and training settings in Appendix A, generation timing, source information and access links are unchanged. The new pose section sketches a procedure without identifying the pose estimator or adding implementation settings or resource-access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds earlier sparse-motion work, including Click to Move and Hao et al.'s Controllable Video Generation with Sparse Trajectories, and discusses I2VControl and Trajectory Attention as specialized architectures. This modestly broadens historical context while retaining the main positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in related work, the embedding explanation and emergent-phenomena discussion, plus small wording and acknowledgement edits. A brief Human Pose Control appendix is inserted before Motion Magnification; the overall narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-row pose-control Fig. A3 and relocates the original motion-magnification figure to the following page as Fig. A4. Several retained images and plots are embedded at higher resolution, with their content unchanged.

improvement.justification: The pose-control examples provide additional qualitative evidence of applicability, and the expanded related work gives more complete credit to earlier trajectory-control research. These are limited gains: quantitative validation remains unchanged, and the new pose demonstration lacks detailed estimator settings and quantitative evaluation.
